cases.sentence: Но когда начал есть, то ___ показался ему чрезвычайно вкусен.
cases.translation: But when he started eating, the dinner seemed extremely tasty to him.
cases.explain: Обед is the subject of показался (seemed), so it is in the nominative case.
The preposition от (from) always governs the genitive case.

cases.sentence: «Так-то, дружок», — сказал Сергей Иванович, трогая его по ___.
cases.translation: 'There now, old fellow,' said Sergei Ivanovich, patting him on the shoulder.
cases.explain: The preposition по (on/along) governs the dative case here.

cases.sentence: Я получил ___ от Доли, она в Юргушове, и у ней что-то все не ладится.
cases.translation: I received a letter from Dolly - she's at Yergushovo, and something isn't going well for her.
cases.explain: Письмо is the direct object of the transitive verb получил (received), so it takes the accusative case.

cases.sentence: Сергей Иванович пил воду с ___ и льдом в своей комнате.
cases.translation: Sergei Ivanovich was drinking water with lemon and ice in his room.
cases.explain: The preposition с (with) governs the instrumental case.

cases.sentence: Сергей Иванович давно уже отобедал и пил воду с лимоном и льдом в своей ___.
cases.translation: Sergei Ivanovich had long since finished dinner and was drinking water with lemon and ice in his room.
cases.explain: The preposition в (in) governs the prepositional case.

reading.ru: Машкин вверх скосили, доделали последние ряды, надели кафтаны и весело пошли к дому.
reading.question: What did the mowers do after finishing Mashkin Verkh?
options: They put on their kaftans and cheerfully headed home
They kept mowing through the night
They went to the river to bathe
reading.correct: They put on their kaftans and cheerfully headed home
reading.explain: The text says they finished the last rows, put on their kaftans, and cheerfully went home.

reading.ru: Сергей Иванович давно уже отобедал и пил воду с лимоном и льдом в своей комнате, просматривая только что полученные с почты газеты и журналы, когда Левин с прилипшими от пота колбу спутанными волосами и почерневшую мокрую спиной и грудью с веселым говором ворвался к нему в комнату.
reading.question: What was Sergei Ivanovich doing when Levin burst into his room?
options: Drinking lemon water with ice and reading newspapers
reading.correct: Drinking lemon water with ice and reading newspapers
reading.explain: The text says he was drinking water with lemon and ice while looking through freshly delivered newspapers and journals.

reading.question: What did Sergei Ivanovich urgently ask Levin to do?
reading.explain: He cries out, 'Shut the door, shut the door!'

reading.question: How did Levin describe his day of mowing to his brother?
reading.explain: Levin says, 'You wouldn't believe what a delight it is.'

reading.ru: Я сейчас приду к тебе», — сказал Сергей Иванович, покачивая головой, глядя на брата.
reading.question: What did Sergei Ivanovich do while looking at his brother?
reading.explain: The text says he spoke while shaking his head, looking at his brother.

reading.ru: Хотя Левину и казалось, что не хочется есть, и он сел за обед только чтобы не обидеть Кузьму, но когда начал есть, то обед показался ему чрезвычайно вкусен.
reading.question: How did Levin end up feeling about the dinner he wasn't hungry for?
options: It turned out to taste extremely delicious once he started eating
He couldn't eat any of it
He gave his portion to Kuzma
He fell asleep at the table
reading.correct: It turned out to taste extremely delicious once he started eating
reading.explain: The text says once he began eating, the dinner seemed extremely tasty to him.

reading.ru: Я получил письмо от Доли, она в Юргушове, и у ней что-то все не ладится.
reading.question: What did Oblonsky's letter say about Dolly?
options: That she was at Yergushovo and something was not going well for her
That she was coming to visit Levin
That she had left for abroad
That she was ill in Moscow
reading.correct: That she was at Yergushovo and something was not going well for her
reading.explain: The letter says he received word from Dolly, who is at Yergushovo, where things are not going well.

reading.ru: Непременно съезжу к ним», — сказал Левин.
reading.question: How did Levin respond to Oblonsky's request to help Dolly?
options: He said he would definitely go visit her
He refused, saying he was too busy
He said his brother should go instead
reading.correct: He said he would definitely go visit her
reading.explain: Levin says, 'I'll definitely go see them.'

reading.ru: Ты не поверишь, какой это режим, полезный против всякой дури!» Я хочу обогатить медицину новым термином — arbeidskur.
reading.question: What term did Levin jokingly want to enrich medicine with?
reading.explain: Levin says he wants to enrich medicine with the new term 'arbeidskur.'

reading.ru: Вообще, мне кажется, что в понятии народном очень твердо определены требования на известную, как они называют, господскую деятельность.
reading.question: What did Sergei Ivanovich say about peasants' views of proper gentlemanly activity?
options: That the common people had firm, defined expectations of what counts as proper gentlemanly activity
That peasants had no opinion on the matter
That peasants encouraged gentlemen to do physical labor
That peasants were indifferent to class distinctions
reading.correct: That the common people had firm, defined expectations of what counts as proper gentlemanly activity
reading.explain: Sergei Ivanovich says the popular conception firmly defines what counts as proper gentlemanly activity.

reading.ru: Это ты не можешь себе представить, что за прелесть.
reading.question: How did Levin describe his day and the old peasant he befriended?
reading.explain: Levin says, 'You can't imagine what a delight it was.'

reading.ru: Левин слушал брата и решительно ничего не понимал.
reading.question: How much did Levin understand of his brother's philosophical explanation?
options: He argued back point by point
reading.explain: The text says Levin listened to his brother and understood absolutely nothing.

reading.ru: «Ах, батюшки!» — вскрикнул Левин так громко, что Сергей Иванович испугался.
reading.question: Why did Levin suddenly cry out loudly, startling Sergei Ivanovich?
options: He remembered Agafya Mikhailovna's injured hand, which he had forgotten
He remembered he'd left the horse untied
He realized he was late for an appointment
reading.correct: He remembered Agafya Mikhailovna's injured hand, which he had forgotten
reading.explain: Levin cries out because he suddenly remembers he forgot about Agafya Mikhailovna's hand.
